source.text: וַיְהִ֗י אַֽחֲרֵי֙ מ֣וֹת שָׁא֔וּל וְדָוִ֣ד שָׁ֔ב מֵהַכּ֖וֹת אֶת־הָעֲמָלֵ֑ק וַיֵּ֧שֶׁב דָּוִ֛ד בְּצִקְלָ֖ג יָמִ֥ים שְׁנָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was after [the] death of Saul, and David had returned from striking the Amalekites, and stayed David in Ziklag days two.

en.L: And it happened after the death of Saul, when David had returned from striking down the Amalekites, that David stayed in Ziklag two days.
en.B: After the death of Saul, when David had come back from defeating the Amalekites, David stayed in Ziklag for two days.
en.R: Saul was now dead. David had come back from beating the Amalekites in battle, and he stayed in the town of Ziklag for two days.

es.L: Y sucedió después de la muerte de Saúl, cuando David había vuelto de herir a los amalecitas, que David se quedó en Siclag dos días.
es.B: Después de la muerte de Saúl, cuando David había regresado de derrotar a los amalecitas, David se quedó dos días en Siclag.
es.R: Saúl ya había muerto. David había vuelto de vencer en batalla a los amalecitas, y se quedó dos días en el pueblo de Siclag.

fr.L: Et il arriva, après la mort de Saül, quand David fut revenu de frapper les Amalécites, que David resta à Tsiqlag deux jours.
fr.B: Après la mort de Saül, quand David fut revenu de sa victoire sur les Amalécites, il resta deux jours à Tsiqlag.
fr.R: Saül était mort. David était revenu après avoir battu les Amalécites, et il est resté deux jours dans la ville de Tsiqlag.

sw.L: Ikawa baada ya kifo cha Sauli, Daudi alipokuwa amerudi kutoka kuwapiga Waamaleki, Daudi akakaa Siklagi siku mbili.
sw.B: Baada ya kifo cha Sauli, Daudi alipokuwa amerudi kutoka kuwashinda Waamaleki, alikaa Siklagi kwa siku mbili.
sw.R: Sauli alikuwa amekwisha kufa. Daudi alikuwa amerudi kutoka vitani, ambako aliwashinda Waamaleki, naye akakaa katika mji wa Siklagi kwa siku mbili.

vi.L: Sau khi Sau-lơ chết, khi Đa-vít đã trở về từ cuộc đánh giết người A-ma-léc, thì Đa-vít ở lại Xiếc-lác hai ngày.
vi.B: Sau khi Sau-lơ chết, Đa-vít đánh bại người A-ma-léc trở về và ở lại Xiếc-lác hai ngày.
vi.R: Lúc ấy Sau-lơ đã chết. Đa-vít vừa đánh thắng người A-ma-léc trở về, và ông ở lại thị trấn Xiếc-lác hai ngày.

decisions.choice: the setting: just after Saul's death in battle on Mount Gilboa (1 Samuel 31)
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew tradition 1 and 2 Samuel were a single book; it was divided into two later. This book picks up directly where 1 Samuel ends. Saul and three of his sons, Jonathan among them, died when the Philistines defeated Israel on Mount Gilboa (1 Samuel 31:1-6). The opening words echo the start of Joshua ("after the death of Moses", Joshua 1:1) and Judges ("after the death of Joshua", Judges 1:1): a leader's death closes one stage of Israel's story and opens the next.

decisions.choice: David's return from striking the Amalekites: the rescue of Ziklag (1 Samuel 30)
decisions.reason: While Saul was fighting the Philistines, David was pursuing the Amalekite raiders who had burned Ziklag and taken its families captive. He struck them down and brought everyone back (1 Samuel 30:1-20). The two battles happened at about the same time, far apart: Saul's in the north, David's in the south.

decisions.choice: Ziklag: the town in the south that the Philistine king Achish gave David
decisions.reason: Achish king of Gath gave David Ziklag while David was living among the Philistines to escape Saul (1 Samuel 27:6). It was the home of David and his men until he moved to Hebron (2:1-3).

decisions.choice: Saul was now dead. ... in the town of Ziklag
decisions.reason: Readable turns the time clause into a short sentence of its own and says that Ziklag was a town.

decisions.choice: passé simple for the narrative at Literal and Balanced ("il arriva", "resta"); passé composé at Readable ("il est resté"); speech in the tenses of speech at every level, including the stories people tell inside it
decisions.reason: For the whole of 2 Samuel, as the French style guide and the Samuel terms note set: the passé simple is the tense of written French narrative, the passé composé the tense of spoken French and of the plain Readable level. The Amalekite's account (verses 6-10) and David's lament (19-27) are speech, so they use the passé composé at every level.

decisions.choice: "Saúl", "David", "los amalecitas", "Siclag"
decisions.reason: For the whole of 2 Samuel, the names follow the Samuel terms note and the Spanish Pentateuch and Psalm titles: "Saúl", "Jonatán", "los amalecitas", "Siclag", "los filisteos", "Gat". Narrative is in the preterite at every level, as the Pentateuch note sets for Spanish.

decisions.choice: Sauli alikuwa amekwisha kufa ... katika mji wa Siklagi
decisions.reason: As the English Readable, the time clause becomes its own short sentence, and Ziklag is called a town ("mji").

decisions.choice: "Sau-lơ", "Đa-vít", "Xiếc-lác", "người A-ma-léc"
decisions.reason: The names keep the forms of the Samuel terms note and the Vietnamese New Testament; David is "ông" in the narration, as Genesis narrates of its heads of households.

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י׀בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֗י וְהִנֵּה֩ אִ֨ישׁ בָּ֤א מִן־הַֽמַּחֲנֶה֙ מֵעִ֣ם שָׁא֔וּל וּבְגָדָ֣יו קְרֻעִ֔ים וַאֲדָמָ֖ה עַל־רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַיְהִי֙ בְּבֹא֣וֹ אֶל־דָּוִ֔ד וַיִּפֹּ֥ל אַ֖רְצָה וַיִּשְׁתָּֽחוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was on the day the third, and look, a man coming from the camp, from with Saul, and his garments torn, and earth on his head; and it was when he came to David, and he fell to [the] ground and bowed down.

en.L: And it happened on the third day, and look, a man came from the camp, from Saul, with his clothes torn and earth on his head. And when he came to David, he fell to the ground and bowed down.
en.B: On the third day a man arrived from Saul's camp. His clothes were torn, and there was dirt on his head. When he came to David, he threw himself to the ground and bowed low.
en.R: On the third day a man came from Saul's army camp. His clothes were torn, and there was dirt on his head to show his sorrow. When he came to David, he bowed down with his face to the ground.

es.L: Y sucedió al tercer día, y he aquí que un hombre vino del campamento, de con Saúl, con la ropa rasgada y tierra sobre la cabeza. Y cuando llegó a David, cayó a tierra y se postró.
es.B: Al tercer día llegó un hombre del campamento de Saúl. Traía la ropa rasgada y tierra sobre la cabeza. Cuando llegó ante David, se echó al suelo y se inclinó profundamente.
es.R: Al tercer día llegó un hombre del campamento del ejército de Saúl. Tenía la ropa rasgada y tierra en la cabeza en señal de dolor. Cuando llegó ante David, se inclinó con el rostro en tierra.

fr.L: Et il arriva le troisième jour, et voici, un homme vint du camp, d’auprès de Saül, les vêtements déchirés et de la terre sur la tête. Et quand il arriva auprès de David, il tomba à terre et se prosterna.
fr.B: Le troisième jour, un homme arriva du camp de Saül. Ses vêtements étaient déchirés et il avait de la terre sur la tête. Quand il parvint auprès de David, il se jeta à terre et se prosterna.
fr.R: Le troisième jour, un homme est arrivé du camp de l’armée de Saül. Ses vêtements étaient déchirés et il avait de la terre sur la tête pour montrer son chagrin. Quand il est arrivé devant David, il s’est incliné, le visage contre le sol.

sw.L: Ikawa siku ya tatu, na tazama, mtu akaja kutoka kambini, kutoka kwa Sauli, mavazi yake yameraruliwa na udongo juu ya kichwa chake. Ikawa alipofika kwa Daudi, akaanguka chini akasujudu.
sw.B: Siku ya tatu mtu mmoja alifika kutoka kambi ya Sauli. Mavazi yake yalikuwa yameraruka, na kichwani mwake palikuwa na mavumbi. Alipomfikia Daudi, alijitupa chini, akasujudu.
sw.R: Siku ya tatu mtu mmoja alikuja kutoka kambi ya jeshi la Sauli. Nguo zake zilikuwa zimeraruka, na kichwani alikuwa na mavumbi kuonyesha huzuni yake. Alipomfikia Daudi, aliinama mpaka uso wake ukagusa ardhi.

vi.L: Đến ngày thứ ba, kìa, có một người từ trại quân, từ chỗ Sau-lơ đến, áo xống xé rách, đầu đầy đất. Khi đến gặp Đa-vít, người ấy sấp mình xuống đất và lạy.
vi.B: Đến ngày thứ ba, có một người từ trại quân của Sau-lơ đến. Áo người ấy rách, đầu dính đầy đất. Khi đến trước mặt Đa-vít, người ấy sấp mình xuống đất mà lạy.
vi.R: Đến ngày thứ ba, có một người từ trại quân của Sau-lơ đến. Áo người ấy bị xé rách, trên đầu có đất để tỏ lòng buồn rầu. Khi đến gặp Đa-vít, người ấy cúi sấp mặt xuống đất.

decisions.choice: torn clothes and earth on the head: signs of mourning
decisions.reason: People tore their clothes and put dust or earth on their heads at news of death or disaster. A runner from the battle at Aphek came to Shiloh looking just the same (1 Samuel 4:12), so David can see at once that the man brings bad news.

decisions.choice: fell to the ground and bowed down: deep respect, the honor given to a ruler
decisions.reason: Bowing to the ground was how one honored a king or a great man (1 Samuel 24:9; 25:23). The man comes from Saul's camp and treats David as if he were already king; in verse 10 he calls him "my lord".

decisions.choice: the third day: counted from David's return to Ziklag
decisions.reason: Verse 1 says David had been in Ziklag two days; the man arrives on the next day.

decisions.choice: to show his sorrow
decisions.reason: Readable adds what the torn clothes and the dirt meant (m1), as at 1 Samuel 4:12.

decisions.choice: "he aquí que"
decisions.reason: In narrative the Literal level renders the Hebrew "look" with "he aquí", as the Spanish terms set for narrative; "mira" is kept for speech.

decisions.choice: kuonyesha huzuni yake
decisions.reason: Readable adds what the torn clothes and the dust meant, as the English Readable does ("to show his sorrow").

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ דָּוִ֔ד אֵ֥י מִזֶּ֖ה תָּב֑וֹא וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו מִמַּחֲנֵ֥ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נִמְלָֽטְתִּי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him David, Where from this do you come? And he said to him, From [the] camp of Israel I have escaped.

en.L: And David said to him, "Where do you come from?" And he said to him, "I have escaped from the camp of Israel."
en.B: David asked him, "Where have you come from?" He answered, "I have escaped from the camp of Israel."
en.R: David asked him, "Where have you come from?" The man said, "I got away from Israel's army camp."

es.L: Y le dijo David: «¿De dónde vienes?». Y él le dijo: «Del campamento de Israel he escapado».
es.B: David le preguntó: «¿De dónde vienes?». Él respondió: «He escapado del campamento de Israel».
es.R: David le preguntó: «¿De dónde vienes?». El hombre contestó: «Logré escapar del campamento del ejército de Israel».

fr.L: Et David lui dit : « D’où viens-tu ? » Et il lui dit : « Je me suis échappé du camp d’Israël. »
fr.B: David lui demanda : « D’où viens-tu ? » Il répondit : « Je me suis échappé du camp d’Israël. »
fr.R: David lui a demandé : « D’où viens-tu ? » L’homme a dit : « Je me suis sauvé du camp de l’armée d’Israël. »

sw.L: Daudi akamwambia, "Unatoka wapi?" Akamwambia, "Nimetoroka kutoka kambi ya Israeli."
sw.B: Daudi akamwuliza, "Umetoka wapi?" Akajibu, "Nimetoroka kutoka kambi ya Israeli."
sw.R: Daudi akamwuliza, "Umetoka wapi?" Yule mtu akasema, "Nimeponyoka kutoka kambi ya jeshi la Israeli."

vi.L: Đa-vít hỏi người ấy: "Ngươi từ đâu đến?" Người ấy thưa: "Tôi vừa thoát khỏi trại quân Y-sơ-ra-ên."
vi.B: Đa-vít hỏi: "Ngươi từ đâu đến?" Người ấy thưa: "Tôi đã thoát ra khỏi trại quân Y-sơ-ra-ên."
vi.R: Đa-vít hỏi: "Ngươi từ đâu đến?" Người ấy đáp: "Tôi vừa chạy thoát khỏi trại quân Y-sơ-ra-ên."

decisions.choice: I have escaped: I got away alive from the defeat
decisions.reason: The verb is used of slipping away from danger with one's life (1 Samuel 19:10-12). The word already tells David that something has gone badly wrong for Israel's army.

decisions.choice: quotation marks «» with “ ” inside and ‘ ’ inside those; a question inside a quotation takes «¿...?»
decisions.reason: For the whole of 2 Samuel, as in the Spanish Pentateuch and New Testament: speech takes the Spanish angle quotes, and a speech that runs across several verses is not closed at each verse.

decisions.choice: David says "ngươi" (and "ta") to the messenger, who answers with "tôi" and "thưa"
decisions.reason: David is a leader of men speaking to a stranger of lower rank who comes to him as to a king (verse 2); the messenger speaks up to him. Kept through the scene.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֥יו דָּוִ֛ד מֶה־הָיָ֥ה הַדָּבָ֖ר הַגֶּד־נָ֣א לִ֑י וַ֠יֹּאמֶר אֲשֶׁר־נָ֨ס הָעָ֜ם מִן־הַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה וְגַם־הַרְבֵּ֞ה נָפַ֤ל מִן־הָעָם֙ וַיָּמֻ֔תוּ וְגַ֗ם שָׁא֛וּל וִיהוֹנָתָ֥ן בְּנ֖וֹ מֵֽתוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him David, What was the word? Tell, please, to me. And he said that fled the people from the battle, and also many fell from the people and died, and also Saul and Jonathan his son died.

en.L: And David said to him, "What was the matter? Tell me, please." And he said, "The people fled from the battle, and also many of the people fell and died, and also Saul and Jonathan his son are dead."
en.B: David said to him, "What happened? Please tell me." He said, "The troops fled from the battle, and many of them fell and died. Saul and his son Jonathan are dead too."
en.R: "What happened?" David asked. "Please tell me." The man said, "The army ran away from the battle. Many of the soldiers were killed. Saul and his son Jonathan are dead too."

es.L: Y le dijo David: «¿Qué pasó? Cuéntamelo, te ruego». Y él dijo: «El pueblo huyó de la batalla, y también muchos del pueblo cayeron y murieron, y también Saúl y Jonatán su hijo han muerto».
es.B: David le dijo: «¿Qué sucedió? Por favor, cuéntamelo». Él dijo: «Las tropas huyeron de la batalla, y muchos de ellos cayeron y murieron. También han muerto Saúl y su hijo Jonatán».
es.R: «¿Qué pasó?», preguntó David. «Por favor, dímelo». El hombre respondió: «El ejército huyó de la batalla. Muchos soldados murieron. También han muerto Saúl y su hijo Jonatán».

fr.L: Et David lui dit : « Quelle a été l’affaire ? Raconte-moi, je te prie. » Et il dit : « Le peuple s’est enfui de la bataille, et aussi beaucoup du peuple sont tombés et sont morts, et aussi Saül et Jonathan son fils sont morts. »
fr.B: David lui dit : « Que s’est-il passé ? Raconte-moi, je t’en prie. » Il répondit : « Les troupes ont fui le combat, et beaucoup d’entre elles sont tombées et sont mortes. Saül et son fils Jonathan sont morts, eux aussi. »
fr.R: « Que s’est-il passé ? a demandé David. Raconte-moi, s’il te plaît. » L’homme a dit : « L’armée s’est enfuie pendant la bataille. Beaucoup de soldats ont été tués. Saül et son fils Jonathan sont morts, eux aussi. »

sw.L: Daudi akamwambia, "Jambo lilikuwa nini? Tafadhali niambie." Akasema, "Watu wamekimbia kutoka vitani, tena wengi wa watu wameanguka wakafa, tena Sauli na Yonathani mwanawe wamekufa."
sw.B: Daudi akamwambia, "Ni nini kilichotokea? Tafadhali niambie." Akasema, "Askari wamekimbia vitani, na wengi wao wameanguka wakafa. Sauli na mwanawe Yonathani nao wamekufa."
sw.R: Daudi akauliza, "Nini kimetokea? Tafadhali niambie." Yule mtu akasema, "Jeshi limekimbia vitani. Askari wengi wameuawa. Sauli na mwanawe Yonathani nao wamekufa."

vi.L: Đa-vít hỏi người ấy: "Sự việc thế nào? Hãy kể cho ta nghe." Người ấy thưa: "Quân lính đã chạy trốn khỏi trận chiến, và cũng có nhiều người trong dân đã ngã xuống và chết; Sau-lơ và Giô-na-than con trai người cũng đã chết."
vi.B: Đa-vít nói: "Việc gì đã xảy ra? Hãy kể cho ta nghe." Người ấy thưa: "Quân lính đã bỏ chạy khỏi trận chiến, nhiều người ngã xuống và chết. Sau-lơ và Giô-na-than con trai vua cũng đã chết."
vi.R: Đa-vít hỏi: "Việc gì đã xảy ra? Hãy kể cho ta nghe." Người ấy đáp: "Quân ta đã bỏ chạy khỏi trận chiến. Nhiều binh lính đã bị giết. Sau-lơ và Giô-na-than con trai vua cũng đã chết."

decisions.choice: What was the word?: What happened? How did it go?
decisions.reason: "Word" here means a matter or event, as when Eli asked the runner from Aphek the same question (1 Samuel 4:16).

decisions.choice: the people: the army in the field
decisions.reason: The word for people often means the fighting men of Israel when they are at war (1 Samuel 4:3-4; 14:15).

decisions.choice: the report builds to its worst news: rout, many dead, and then Saul and Jonathan
decisions.reason: Each clause begins with "and also", so the news grows heavier step by step and ends with the deaths that matter most to David: the king and David's close friend.

decisions.choice: the troops, them (Balanced); the army, the soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: As across Samuel and Kings, "the people" meaning an army is "the troops" at Balanced and "the army" or "the soldiers" at Readable (m2).

decisions.choice: les troupes (B); l'armée, les soldats (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole of 2 Samuel: "the people" meaning the army in the field (m2) is "le peuple" at Literal, "les troupes" at Balanced and "l'armée" or "les soldats" at Readable, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "el pueblo" (L); "las tropas" (B); "el ejército", "soldados" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English across Samuel: "the people" meaning the army in the field is "el pueblo" at Literal, "las tropas" at Balanced and "el ejército" or "los soldados" at Readable.

decisions.choice: askari (Balanced); jeshi, askari (Readable)
decisions.reason: As the English, "the people" meaning the army in the field is "askari" (troops) at Balanced and "jeshi" or "askari" at Readable; Literal keeps "watu".

decisions.choice: "quân lính", "dân" (L); "quân lính" (B); "quân ta", "binh lính" (R)
decisions.reason: "The people" here means the army in the field (meaning decision), so Balanced and Readable name the soldiers.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔ד אֶל־הַנַּ֖עַר הַמַּגִּ֣יד ל֑וֹ אֵ֣יךְ יָדַ֔עְתָּ כִּי־מֵ֥ת שָׁא֖וּל וִיהֽוֹנָתָ֥ן בְּנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said David to the young man who told to him, How do you know that died Saul and Jonathan his son?

en.L: And David said to the young man who was telling him, "How do you know that Saul and Jonathan his son are dead?"
en.B: Then David said to the young man who had brought the news, "How do you know that Saul is dead, and his son Jonathan?"
en.R: David asked the young man who had brought the news, "How can you tell that Saul and his son Jonathan have died?"

es.L: Y dijo David al joven que le estaba informando: «¿Cómo sabes que han muerto Saúl y Jonatán su hijo?».
es.B: Entonces David le dijo al joven que le había traído la noticia: «¿Cómo sabes que Saúl ha muerto, y también su hijo Jonatán?».
es.R: David le preguntó al joven que le había traído la noticia: «¿Cómo puedes saber que Saúl y su hijo Jonatán han muerto?».

fr.L: Et David dit au jeune homme qui le renseignait : « Comment sais-tu que Saül et Jonathan son fils sont morts ? »
fr.B: Alors David dit au jeune homme qui lui avait apporté la nouvelle : « Comment sais-tu que Saül est mort, et son fils Jonathan ? »
fr.R: David a demandé au jeune homme qui avait apporté la nouvelle : « Comment peux-tu savoir que Saül et son fils Jonathan sont morts ? »

sw.L: Daudi akamwambia yule kijana aliyekuwa akimpa habari, "Unajuaje kwamba Sauli na Yonathani mwanawe wamekufa?"
sw.B: Kisha Daudi akamwambia yule kijana aliyemletea habari, "Unajuaje kwamba Sauli amekufa, na mwanawe Yonathani?"
sw.R: Daudi akamwuliza yule kijana aliyemletea habari, "Unawezaje kujua kwamba Sauli na mwanawe Yonathani wamekufa?"

vi.L: Đa-vít hỏi người thanh niên đang báo tin cho mình: "Làm sao ngươi biết Sau-lơ và Giô-na-than con trai người đã chết?"
vi.B: Bấy giờ Đa-vít hỏi người thanh niên đã đem tin đến: "Làm sao ngươi biết Sau-lơ đã chết, cả Giô-na-than con trai người nữa?"
vi.R: Đa-vít hỏi người thanh niên đã báo tin: "Làm sao ngươi biết chắc Sau-lơ và Giô-na-than con trai người đã chết?"

decisions.choice: the young man: a young man, perhaps a servant or soldier
decisions.reason: The word means a youth or young man and is often used of a servant or an attendant in war, such as an armor-bearer (1 Samuel 14:1). It does not say what his place in Saul's army was.

decisions.choice: How do you know?: David asks for proof

decisions.choice: the man's account differs from the narrator's in 1 Samuel 31: he is most likely lying to win David's favor
alternatives: the man found Saul still alive after he fell on his sword and finished him
decisions.reason: 1 Samuel 31:3-5 says that Saul was badly wounded by archers and, when his armor-bearer would not kill him, fell on his own sword. This man says he found Saul leaning on his spear with the enemy closing in, and that he killed him at Saul's own request (verses 9-10). The narrator's account in 1 Samuel 31 is the one the book itself gives as what happened, and the man has an obvious motive: he brings Saul's crown to David and expects a reward. David later says as much: the man thought he was bringing good news, and David's answer was to have him killed (4:10). Some readers have tried to fit the two accounts together, supposing that Saul's fall on his sword did not kill him at once and that the Amalekite then finished him. The text does not say so, and nothing in 1 Samuel 31 leaves room for a second man.

decisions.choice: I happened by chance: the man stresses that he was there by accident

decisions.choice: the chariots and the masters of horsemen: the Philistine chariot force and its horsemen

decisions.choice: and there was Saul ... while the chariots

sw.B: Ndipo Daudi akashika mavazi yake akayararua, na watu wote waliokuwa pamoja naye wakafanya vivyo hivyo.
sw.R: Ndipo Daudi akashika nguo zake akazirarua kuonyesha huzuni yake. Watu wake wote wakafanya vivyo hivyo.

vi.L: Đa-vít nắm lấy áo mình mà xé ra, và tất cả những người ở với ông cũng làm vậy.
vi.B: Bấy giờ Đa-vít nắm lấy áo mình mà xé ra, và tất cả những người đi theo ông cũng làm như vậy.
vi.R: Đa-vít liền nắm lấy áo mình mà xé ra để tỏ lòng đau buồn. Tất cả những người theo ông cũng làm như thế.

decisions.choice: tearing one's clothes: the act of a mourner
decisions.reason: Tearing the clothes was the first, sudden sign of grief at news of death or disaster (Genesis 37:34; Joshua 7:6). David does not rejoice that his pursuer is dead; he and his men mourn at once.

decisions.choice: his clothes
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text read "his garment" (one), and the form marked to be read aloud is "his garments". The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: to show his sorrow
decisions.reason: Readable adds what tearing the clothes meant (m1).

source.text: וַֽיִּסְפְּדוּ֙ וַיִּבְכּ֔וּ וַיָּצֻ֖מוּ עַד־הָעָ֑רֶב עַל־שָׁא֞וּל וְעַל־יְהוֹנָתָ֣ן בְּנ֗וֹ וְעַל־עַ֤ם יְהוָה֙ וְעַל־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֥י נָפְל֖וּ בֶּחָֽרֶב׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they mourned and wept and fasted until the evening for Saul and for Jonathan his son and for [the] people of Yahweh and for [the] house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.

en.L: And they mourned and wept and fasted until the evening for Saul and for Jonathan his son and for the people of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and for the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.
en.B: They mourned and wept and went without food until evening for Saul and his son Jonathan, for the people of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the house of Israel, since they had fallen by the sword.
en.R: They cried and mourned and did not eat until evening. They grieved for Saul and his son Jonathan, for the people of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and for the nation of Israel, because so many had been killed in battle.

es.L: Y se lamentaron y lloraron y ayunaron hasta la tarde por Saúl y por Jonatán su hijo y por el pueblo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y por la casa de Israel, porque habían caído a espada.
es.B: Hicieron duelo, lloraron y no comieron nada hasta la tarde por Saúl y su hijo Jonatán, por el pueblo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y por la casa de Israel, ya que habían caído a espada.
es.R: Lloraron e hicieron duelo, y no comieron hasta la tarde. Sintieron gran dolor por Saúl y su hijo Jonatán, por el pueblo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y por la nación de Israel, porque muchos habían muerto en la batalla.

fr.L: Et ils se lamentèrent, pleurèrent et jeûnèrent jusqu’au soir sur Saül et sur Jonathan son fils, et sur le peuple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et sur la maison d’Israël, parce qu’ils étaient tombés par l’épée.
fr.B: Ils se lamentèrent, pleurèrent et restèrent sans manger jusqu’au soir pour Saül et son fils Jonathan, pour le peuple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et pour la maison d’Israël, car ils étaient tombés par l’épée.
fr.R: Ils ont pleuré et se sont lamentés, et ils n’ont rien mangé jusqu’au soir. Ils étaient en deuil pour Saül et son fils Jonathan, pour le peuple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et pour la nation d’Israël, parce que tant d’hommes avaient été tués au combat.

sw.L: Wakaomboleza, wakalia, wakafunga mpaka jioni kwa ajili ya Sauli na kwa ajili ya Yonathani mwanawe, na kwa ajili ya watu wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na kwa ajili ya nyumba ya Israeli, kwa sababu walikuwa wameanguka kwa upanga.
sw.B: Waliomboleza, wakalia, wakakaa bila kula mpaka jioni kwa ajili ya Sauli na mwanawe Yonathani, kwa ajili ya watu wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na nyumba ya Israeli, kwa kuwa walikuwa wameanguka kwa upanga.
sw.R: Walilia na kuomboleza, wala hawakula chochote mpaka jioni. Waliwaombolezea Sauli na mwanawe Yonathani, watu wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na taifa la Israeli, kwa sababu wengi walikuwa wameuawa vitani.

vi.L: Họ than khóc, kêu khóc và kiêng ăn cho đến chiều vì Sau-lơ, vì Giô-na-than con trai người, vì dân của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và vì nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên, bởi họ đã ngã xuống dưới lưỡi gươm.
vi.B: Họ than khóc, kêu khóc và nhịn ăn cho đến chiều vì Sau-lơ và Giô-na-than con trai người, vì dân của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên, vì họ đã ngã chết dưới lưỡi gươm.
vi.R: Họ khóc lóc, than thở và không ăn gì cho đến chiều. Họ thương tiếc Sau-lơ và Giô-na-than con trai người, thương tiếc dân của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và cả dân tộc Y-sơ-ra-ên, vì quá nhiều người đã bị giết trong trận chiến.

decisions.choice: mourned, wept and fasted until evening: a day of public mourning
decisions.reason: Mourning was loud and public, and fasting until evening set the whole day apart for grief. The men of Jabesh-gilead fasted seven days for Saul (1 Samuel 31:13).

decisions.choice: the people of the LORD and the house of Israel: the same nation named twice
decisions.reason: Both phrases mean Israel, first as the people who belong to the LORD and then as one family descended from Israel. The mourning reaches beyond Saul and Jonathan to all who died in the defeat (verse 4).

decisions.choice: fallen by the sword: killed in battle
decisions.reason: "The sword" stands for war and violent death; it does not mean that every man died by a sword blow.

decisions.choice: went without food, did not eat; the nation of Israel (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what fasting was. Readable says "the nation of Israel" for "the house of Israel" (m2) and "killed in battle" for "fallen by the sword" (m3).

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}: "le SEIGNEUR" in capitals, with the name "Yahvé" as the reader setting
decisions.reason: For the whole of 2 Samuel, as the Pentateuch and Samuel terms notes set: the divine name is "le SEIGNEUR", like the English "the LORD"; the span takes in the article and its contraction so that both options read naturally. "L'Éternel", the Segond tradition, is the alternative a reviewer may prefer.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}
decisions.reason: For the whole of 2 Samuel, as in the Spanish Pentateuch: the divine name is "el SEÑOR" in small capitals by default, like the English "the LORD", with "Yahvé" as the reader setting; the span takes in the article and its contraction ("del SEÑOR|de Yahvé", "al SEÑOR|a Yahvé").

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}
decisions.reason: Throughout 2 Samuel the divine name is BWANA in capitals, with "Yahwe" as the reader's alternative, as in the Pentateuch and Psalms.

decisions.choice: "kiêng ăn" (L); "nhịn ăn" (B); "không ăn gì" (R)
decisions.reason: "ăn chay" today means a meatless diet; the fast here was going without food, so Balanced and Readable say so plainly.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗ד אֶל־הַנַּ֨עַר֙ הַמַּגִּ֣יד ל֔וֹ אֵ֥י מִזֶּ֖ה אָ֑תָּה וַיֹּ֕אמֶר בֶּן־אִ֛ישׁ גֵּ֥ר עֲמָלֵקִ֖י אָנֹֽכִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said David to the young man who told to him, Where from this [are] you? And he said, [The] son of a man, a sojourner, an Amalekite I [am].

en.L: And David said to the young man who had told him, "Where [are] you from?" And he said, "I [am] the son of a sojourner, an Amalekite."
en.B: David said to the young man who had brought him the news, "Where are you from?" He answered, "I am the son of an outsider who lives among you, an Amalekite."
en.R: David asked the young man who had brought the news, "Where are you from?" He answered, "My father was an Amalekite who came to live in Israel."

es.L: Y dijo David al joven que le había informado: «¿De dónde [eres] tú?». Y él dijo: «Hijo de un inmigrante, un amalecita, [soy] yo».
es.B: David le preguntó al joven que le había traído la noticia: «¿De dónde eres?». Él respondió: «Soy hijo de un extranjero que vive aquí, un amalecita».
es.R: David le preguntó al joven que le había traído la noticia: «¿De dónde eres?». Él contestó: «Mi padre era un amalecita que vino a vivir a Israel».

fr.L: Et David dit au jeune homme qui l’avait renseigné : « D’où [es]-tu ? » Et il dit : « Je [suis] le fils d’un immigré, un Amalécite. »
fr.B: David dit au jeune homme qui lui avait apporté la nouvelle : « D’où es-tu ? » Il répondit : « Je suis le fils d’un étranger établi parmi vous, un Amalécite. »
fr.R: David a demandé au jeune homme qui avait apporté la nouvelle : « D’où es-tu ? » Il a répondu : « Mon père était un Amalécite venu vivre en Israël. »

sw.L: Daudi akamwambia yule kijana aliyempa habari, "Wewe [ni] wa wapi?" Akasema, "Mimi [ni] mwana wa mtu mgeni, Mwamaleki."
sw.B: Daudi akamwambia yule kijana aliyemletea habari, "Wewe ni wa wapi?" Akajibu, "Mimi ni mwana wa mgeni anayeishi kati yenu, Mwamaleki."
sw.R: Daudi akamwuliza yule kijana aliyemletea habari, "Wewe ni wa wapi?" Akajibu, "Baba yangu alikuwa Mwamaleki aliyekuja kuishi katika Israeli."

vi.L: Đa-vít hỏi người thanh niên đã báo tin cho mình: "Ngươi từ đâu đến?" Người ấy thưa: "Tôi là con trai của một ngoại kiều, một người A-ma-léc."
vi.B: Đa-vít hỏi người thanh niên đã đem tin đến: "Ngươi là người ở đâu?" Người ấy thưa: "Tôi là con của một người ngoại quốc sống giữa dân Y-sơ-ra-ên, một người A-ma-léc."
vi.R: Đa-vít hỏi người thanh niên đã báo tin: "Ngươi là người ở đâu?" Người ấy thưa: "Cha tôi là một người A-ma-léc đến sống ở Y-sơ-ra-ên."

decisions.choice: the son of a sojourner: a man whose family had settled in Israel without belonging to it by birth
decisions.reason: A sojourner was someone living among Israel who was not an Israelite, under the protection of Israel's laws and bound by many of them (Leviticus 24:22; Numbers 15:15-16). So this man was no stranger to Israel's ways: he would have known who Saul was and what it meant to strike the LORD's anointed (verse 14).

decisions.choice: Where are you from?: a question about his people, not his route
decisions.reason: In verse 3 David asked where he had come from that day. Now he asks about the man himself, and the answer is his family and people. The question is the first step of a trial (verses 14-16).

decisions.choice: sojourner (Literal); an outsider who lives among you (Balanced); came to live in Israel (Readable)
decisions.reason: As across these books, the word is "sojourner" at Literal and "outsider" at Balanced. Readable explains it as someone who came to live in Israel and makes the father the subject.

decisions.choice: un immigré (L); un étranger établi parmi vous (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is the one for a resident foreigner (m1), "l'étranger, l'immigré" in the Pentateuch terms list. Literal uses "immigré"; Balanced follows the English "an outsider who lives among you".

decisions.choice: "inmigrante" (L); "un extranjero que vive aquí" (B)
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch terms list for the ger: "inmigrante" at Literal, "extranjero" at Balanced, which says where he lives rather than "among you", since the man is speaking to David alone.

decisions.choice: mgeni (Literal); mgeni anayeishi kati yenu (Balanced); aliyekuja kuishi katika Israeli (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Mgeni" is the word for the sojourner (*ger*) set for the Pentateuch; Balanced adds that he lived among Israel and Readable explains it, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "ngoại kiều" (L); "người ngoại quốc sống giữa dân Y-sơ-ra-ên" (B); "đến sống ở Y-sơ-ra-ên" (R)
decisions.reason: The sojourner is a foreigner settled among Israel (meaning decision); Balanced says who he was among, Readable makes the father the subject, as the English does.

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֵלָ֖יו דָּוִ֑ד אֵ֚יךְ לֹ֣א יָרֵ֔אתָ לִשְׁלֹ֨חַ֙ יָֽדְךָ֔ לְשַׁחֵ֖ת אֶת־מְשִׁ֥יחַ יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him David, How were you not afraid to stretch out your hand to destroy [the] anointed of Yahweh?

en.L: And David said to him, "How were you not afraid to stretch out your hand to destroy {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed?"
en.B: David said to him, "How is it that you were not afraid to lift your hand to destroy {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed?"
en.R: David said to him, "Why were you not afraid to kill the king {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has anointed?"

es.L: Y le dijo David: «¿Cómo no tuviste miedo de extender tu mano para destruir al ungido {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}?».
es.B: David le dijo: «¿Cómo es que no tuviste miedo de levantar la mano para destruir al ungido {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}?».
es.R: David le dijo: «¿Por qué no tuviste miedo de matar al rey que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha ungido?».

fr.L: Et David lui dit : « Comment n’as-tu pas craint d’étendre ta main pour détruire l’oint {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ? »
fr.B: David lui dit : « Comment se fait-il que tu n’aies pas eu peur de lever la main pour détruire l’oint {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ? »
fr.R: David lui a dit : « Pourquoi n’as-tu pas eu peur de tuer le roi que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a oint ? »

sw.L: Daudi akamwambia, "Ilikuwaje hukuogopa kunyosha mkono wako kumwangamiza masihi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}?"
sw.B: Daudi akamwambia, "Imekuwaje hukuogopa kuinua mkono wako kumwangamiza mfalme wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyempaka mafuta?"
sw.R: Daudi akamwambia, "Kwa nini hukuogopa kumwua mfalme ambaye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amempaka mafuta?"

vi.L: Đa-vít nói với người ấy: "Sao ngươi không sợ khi giơ tay ra giết hại người được xức dầu của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}?"
vi.B: Đa-vít nói với người ấy: "Sao ngươi dám giơ tay giết hại vị vua được {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} xức dầu mà không sợ?"
vi.R: Đa-vít nói với người ấy: "Sao ngươi không sợ khi giết vị vua {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã xức dầu?"

decisions.choice: the LORD's anointed: the king the LORD himself had chosen and set apart
decisions.reason: Saul was anointed with oil by Samuel at the LORD's command (1 Samuel 10:1). Anointing marked the king as the LORD's own, so to harm him was to act against the LORD. David twice had Saul in his power and refused to touch him for this very reason (1 Samuel 24:7, 11; 26:9-11, 23). Now a man boasts of doing what David would not do.

decisions.choice: stretch out your hand: attack, raise your hand against
decisions.reason: The phrase is the one David himself used when he refused to harm Saul (1 Samuel 24:7; 26:9, 11, 23).

decisions.choice: the king the LORD has anointed
decisions.reason: As across Samuel and Kings, Literal and Balanced keep "the LORD's anointed", and Readable says who the anointed one is. Readable also says "kill" for "stretch out your hand to destroy" (m2).

decisions.choice: l'oint du SEIGNEUR (L, B); le roi que le SEIGNEUR a oint (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole of 2 Samuel, as the Samuel terms note sets: "oindre" and "l'oint" keep the link with the anointing of kings; Readable says who the anointed one is, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "el ungido del SEÑOR" (L, B); "el rey que el SEÑOR ha ungido" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note sets for mashiaḥ YHWH, following the English levels.

decisions.choice: masihi wa BWANA (Literal); mfalme wa BWANA aliyempaka mafuta (Balanced); mfalme ambaye BWANA amempaka mafuta (Readable)
decisions.reason: As set for Samuel in Swahili: Literal keeps the noun "masihi" (anointed one), Balanced and Readable say who he is, since "Masihi" alone points a Swahili reader to the Messiah.

decisions.choice: "người được xức dầu của CHÚA" (L); "vị vua được CHÚA xức dầu" (B); "vị vua CHÚA đã xức dầu" (R)
decisions.reason: The forms of the Samuel terms note for *mashiaḥ YHWH*, used through the book: Literal keeps the Hebrew's "anointed one", Balanced and Readable say it is the king.

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֣א דָוִ֗ד לְאַחַד֙ מֵֽהַנְּעָרִ֔ים וַיֹּ֖אמֶר גַּ֣שׁ פְּגַע־בּ֑וֹ וַיַּכֵּ֖הוּ וַיָּמֹֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And called David to one of the young men and said, Draw near, fall on him; and he struck him, and he died.

en.L: And David called one of the young men and said, "Draw near; fall on him." And he struck him, and he died.
en.B: Then David called one of his young men and said, "Go and strike him down!" So he struck him, and the man died.
en.R: Then David called one of his men and said, "Go and kill him!" So the young man struck him, and he died.

es.L: Y llamó David a uno de los jóvenes y dijo: «Acércate, cae sobre él». Y lo hirió, y murió.
es.B: Entonces David llamó a uno de sus jóvenes y le dijo: «¡Ve y mátalo!». Así que lo hirió, y el hombre murió.
es.R: Entonces David llamó a uno de sus hombres y le dijo: «¡Ve y mátalo!». El joven lo hirió, y el hombre murió.

fr.L: Et David appela un des jeunes gens et dit : « Approche, tombe sur lui ! » Et il le frappa, et il mourut.
fr.B: Alors David appela un de ses jeunes gens et lui dit : « Va, abats-le ! » Il le frappa, et l’homme mourut.
fr.R: Alors David a appelé un de ses hommes et lui a dit : « Va le tuer ! » Le jeune homme l’a frappé, et l’Amalécite est mort.

sw.L: Daudi akamwita mmoja wa vijana akasema, "Sogea, mwangukie." Akampiga, naye akafa.
sw.B: Kisha Daudi akamwita mmoja wa vijana wake akasema, "Nenda ukamwangushe!" Basi akampiga, na yule mtu akafa.
sw.R: Kisha Daudi akamwita mmoja wa watu wake akasema, "Nenda ukamwue!" Basi yule kijana akampiga, naye akafa.

vi.L: Đa-vít gọi một trong các thanh niên và nói: "Hãy lại gần, xông vào nó!" Người ấy đánh hắn, và hắn chết.
vi.B: Rồi Đa-vít gọi một trong các thanh niên của mình và bảo: "Hãy đi giết nó!" Người ấy đánh hắn, và hắn chết.
vi.R: Rồi Đa-vít gọi một người lính của mình và bảo: "Hãy đi giết nó!" Người lính đánh hắn, và hắn chết.

decisions.choice: fall on him: attack him, strike him down
decisions.reason: The verb means to meet someone, and in a setting like this to meet him with violence (1 Samuel 22:17-18). David orders the man's death.

decisions.choice: the young men: David's fighting men
decisions.reason: The same word that names the Amalekite (verse 5) is used of the soldiers who served David (1 Samuel 21:3; 25:5).

decisions.choice: the man's death: David's judgment on the killing of the king
decisions.reason: David treats the man's own claim as a confession (verse 16). By punishing it he shows publicly that he had no part in Saul's death and took no pleasure in it. He acts the same way later when Ish-bosheth's murderers bring him their master's head (4:9-12).

decisions.choice: Go and strike him down! (Balanced); Go and kill him! (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Draw near" is a command to go up to the man; Balanced and Readable say "Go" and say what "fall on him" meant (m1).

decisions.choice: "nó", "hắn" for the Amalekite once he is condemned
decisions.reason: Vietnamese marks contempt in its pronouns; once David has judged him, the narration and David's order speak of him as "hắn" and "nó", while his slayer stays "người ấy".

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ דָּוִ֔ד דָּמְךָ֖ עַל־רֹאשֶׁ֑ךָ כִּ֣י פִ֗יךָ עָנָ֤ה בְךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אָנֹכִ֥י מֹתַ֖תִּי אֶת־מְשִׁ֥יחַ יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And said to him David, Your blood [be] on your head, for your mouth has testified against you, saying, I killed [the] anointed of Yahweh.

en.L: And David said to him, "Your blood [is] on your head, for your own mouth has testified against you, saying, 'I killed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed.'"
en.B: David said to him, "Your blood is on your own head, for your own mouth has testified against you when you said, 'I killed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed.'"
en.R: David said to him, "You are to blame for your own death. Your own words prove you guilty, for you said, 'I killed the king {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has anointed.'"

es.L: Y le dijo David: «Tu sangre [sea] sobre tu cabeza, porque tu propia boca ha testificado contra ti, diciendo: “Yo maté al ungido {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}”».
es.B: David le dijo: «Tu sangre caiga sobre tu propia cabeza, porque tu misma boca ha dado testimonio contra ti cuando dijiste: “Yo maté al ungido {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}”».
es.R: David le dijo: «Tú tienes la culpa de tu propia muerte. Tus propias palabras te declaran culpable, porque dijiste: “Yo maté al rey que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha ungido”».

fr.L: Et David lui dit : « Ton sang [est] sur ta tête, car ta bouche a témoigné contre toi, en disant : “J’ai tué l’oint {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.” »
fr.B: David lui avait dit : « Ton sang retombe sur ta propre tête, car ta propre bouche a témoigné contre toi quand tu as dit : “J’ai tué l’oint {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.” »
fr.R: David lui a dit : « Tu es seul responsable de ta mort. Tes propres paroles prouvent que tu es coupable, car tu as dit : “J’ai tué le roi que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a oint.” »

sw.R: Daudi alikuwa amemwambia, "Wewe mwenyewe ndiwe mwenye hatia ya kifo chako. Maneno yako mwenyewe yamekuhukumu, kwa maana ulisema, 'Nimemwua mfalme ambaye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amempaka mafuta.'"

vi.B: Đa-vít đã nói với hắn: "Máu ngươi đổ lại trên đầu ngươi, vì chính miệng ngươi đã làm chứng chống lại ngươi khi nói: 'Tôi đã giết vị vua được {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} xức dầu.'"
vi.R: Đa-vít đã nói với hắn: "Chính ngươi phải chịu trách nhiệm về cái chết của mình. Lời ngươi nói đã chứng minh ngươi có tội, vì ngươi đã nói: 'Tôi đã giết vị vua {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã xức dầu.'"

decisions.choice: your blood is on your head: you are responsible for your own death
decisions.reason: The saying lays the guilt for a death on the one who dies, so that no blame falls on those who carry out the sentence (Joshua 2:19; 1 Kings 2:37).

decisions.choice: David's words come after the report of the man's death but belong with the sentence
decisions.reason: Hebrew stories often tell an outcome and then give the words that went with it. David's sentence was spoken to the man as judgment was passed on him, whether just before he was struck or as it was done.

decisions.choice: your blood
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text read "your bloods" (plural, as in Genesis 4:10), and the form marked to be read aloud is "your blood". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: your own mouth has testified: the man's claim stands as his confession
decisions.reason: David does not try to find out whether the story is true. The man has said in front of witnesses that he killed the LORD's anointed, and David judges him by his own words.

decisions.choice: You are to blame for your own death; Your own words prove you guilty
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom of blood on the head (m1) and says plainly what the mouth testifying meant (m4).

decisions.choice: David lui avait dit (plus-que-parfait)
decisions.reason: The sentence was spoken as judgment was passed, before the death told in verse 15 (m2). French Balanced marks this with the pluperfect; Literal keeps the plain narrative tense of the Hebrew order.

decisions.choice: Daudi alikuwa amemwambia
decisions.reason: The sentence was spoken before or as the man was struck (m2); Balanced and Readable use the past perfect "alikuwa amemwambia" so that the order of events is not misread after "he died" in verse 15.

decisions.choice: Bow: the name of the lament, probably taken from the bow of Jonathan in verse 22
decisions.reason: The single word "Bow" stands after "to teach the sons of Judah" without anything to join it to the sentence. It is most likely the title by which the song was known, as other songs are named by a word in them. Another reading is that David ordered the men of Judah to be taught the use of the bow, since Saul's army had been beaten by archers (1 Samuel 31:3); but the sentence is about the lament, and the words added to make that reading work are not in the text.

decisions.choice: the Book of Jashar: a lost collection of poems, quoted also in Joshua 10:13
decisions.reason: The name means "the book of the upright one". It is quoted for Joshua's words to the sun and moon (Joshua 10:12-13) and here for David's lament. Both are poems about Israel's battles and heroes, so it seems to have been a collection of songs. No copy has survived. The note tells the reader where the song could be found.

decisions.choice: he said to teach: he gave orders that it be taught
decisions.reason: "Said" with "to" and a verb is a command. David wanted the song learned in Judah, his own tribe and soon his kingdom (2:4).

decisions.choice: the Song of the Bow; a book of old songs (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "Song of the" so that the single word reads as a title (m1), and leave out "look", which simply points to the source. Readable explains what the Book of Jashar was (m2), as at Joshua 10:13.

decisions.choice: le livre du Yashar (L); le livre du Juste (B, R)
alternatives: le livre de Yashar at every level
decisions.reason: The name means "the book of the upright one" (m2). Literal keeps the Hebrew name, as the English Literal keeps "Jashar"; Balanced and Readable give its meaning, the usual French name of the book.

decisions.choice: "los hijos de Judá" (L); "la gente de Judá" (B, R), with no gender span; "el libro de Jaser"
decisions.reason: Spanish "hijos" already takes in daughters and "gente" is inclusive, so the English gender span has no second Spanish wording here; the lost book takes the usual Spanish form of its name, as at Joshua 10:13.

decisions.choice: [wimbo wa] Upinde (Literal); Wimbo wa Upinde (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The single word "Bow" is the song's title (m1). Swahili cannot leave it bare after "kuwafundisha", so even Literal supplies "[wimbo wa]" in brackets.

decisions.choice: watu wa Yuda
decisions.reason: The English has a gender span on "sons of Judah". "Watu" already includes men and women and "wana" (Literal) means children of either sex, so Swahili has no span here, as the Pentateuch note sets for "the sons of Israel".

decisions.choice: "con cháu Giu-đa" (L); "người Giu-đa" (B, R), with no gender setting
alternatives: "con trai Giu-đa" as a second wording
decisions.reason: The English sets "sons of Judah" as a gender choice; Vietnamese "con cháu" and "người" already include men and women, so there is no second wording to offer.

decisions.choice: "Sách Gia-sa"
decisions.reason: The book's name is kept as a name; Readable says what kind of book it was, as the English does.

decisions.choice: a lament: a funeral song, set in lines of poetry
decisions.reason: Verses 19-27 are the song David sang (verse 17). It is built of short balanced lines and framed by a cry that comes back three times: "How the mighty have fallen!" (verses 19, 25, 27). "How" here is a cry of grief, the word that opens other laments (Lamentations 1:1; 2:1).

decisions.choice: the splendor: Israel's pride and beauty, meaning Saul and Jonathan
decisions.reason: The word means beauty, glory or splendor (Isaiah 4:2; 13:19). The same letters also spell "gazelle", an animal admired for its speed and grace (2:18), and some read the line as a picture of Jonathan lying like a slain gazelle on the hills. Either way the line mourns the fallen leaders as Israel's finest.

decisions.choice: your heights: the hills of Gilboa where the battle was fought
decisions.reason: The word is often used of hilltop shrines, but here it simply means high ground, the mountain where Saul and Jonathan fell (verse 21; 1 Samuel 31:1). The line is spoken to Israel, whose hills they were.

decisions.choice: the mighty: Israel's warriors, above all Saul and Jonathan
decisions.reason: The word means strong men, heroes of war. "Fallen" means killed in battle (verse 10, m1).

decisions.choice: How the mighty have fallen! (Literal); How the warriors have fallen! (Balanced); How the brave warriors have fallen! (Readable)
decisions.reason: The refrain is drafted afresh at each level. Literal keeps "the mighty", the old and familiar form of the line. Balanced and Readable name who the mighty were, fighting men, using a word that fits both Israel's dead and the enemy warriors of verse 22. The same wording is kept in verses 25 and 27.

decisions.choice: your finest men ... on your hills
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly who Israel's splendor was (m2) and says "hills" for the heights.

decisions.choice: Comment sont tombés les vaillants ! (L); Ils sont tombés, les guerriers ! (B); Ils sont tombés, nos braves guerriers ! (R)
alternatives: Comment les héros sont-ils tombés ! at every level
decisions.reason: The refrain (verses 19, 25, 27) is drafted afresh at each level. Literal keeps the exclamatory "comment"; Balanced and Readable say it as a plain cry, since "Comment ... sont-ils tombés" reads in modern French like a question, and name the mighty as warriors, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "¡Cómo han caído los valientes!" (L); "los guerreros" (B); "los guerreros valientes" (R)
decisions.reason: The refrain of the lament keeps one wording at each level through verses 19, 25 and 27, following the English levels; the lament is set in lines as the English is.

decisions.choice: Jinsi mashujaa walivyoanguka! (Literal); Jinsi wapiganaji walivyoanguka! (Balanced); Jinsi wapiganaji hodari walivyoanguka! (Readable)
decisions.reason: The refrain is drafted afresh at each level, as in English, and kept the same in verses 25 and 27. "Jinsi ... walivyoanguka" carries the cry of grief of "How". Literal keeps "mashujaa" (the mighty); Balanced and Readable name them as fighting men.

decisions.choice: mahali pako pa juu
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for "high places", so Literal keeps "mahali pa juu"; here it means the hills of Gilboa (m3), which Balanced and Readable say.

decisions.choice: "Ôi, [các] dũng sĩ đã ngã xuống!" (L); "Ôi, các chiến binh đã ngã gục!" (B); "Ôi, những chiến binh dũng cảm đã ngã gục!" (R)
alternatives: "Sao các dũng sĩ đã ngã xuống!"
decisions.reason: The refrain (verses 19, 25, 27) is a cry of grief, not a question; Vietnamese opens it with "Ôi" and keeps one wording at each level each time it returns.

decisions.choice: Gath and Ashkelon: two of the five chief Philistine cities
decisions.reason: The Philistines ruled from five cities: Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron (1 Samuel 6:17). Naming two of them stands for the whole Philistine land.

decisions.choice: do not announce it ... the daughters will rejoice: the Philistines' victory celebration
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for carrying good news, and the Philistines had already sent the news of Saul's death through their land (1 Samuel 31:9). Women came out singing to greet victorious armies, as Israel's women sang over Saul and David (1 Samuel 18:6-7). David cannot stop the news; the line grieves that the enemy will sing over Israel's dead.

decisions.choice: the uncircumcised: people outside the covenant the LORD made with Israel
decisions.reason: Circumcision was the sign of the covenant with Abraham's family (Genesis 17:10-11), and Israel called the Philistines "the uncircumcised" as a name for outsiders to that covenant (1 Samuel 14:6; 17:26; 31:4).

decisions.choice: The Philistine women; The women of those outside God's covenant
decisions.reason: "Daughters" here means the women of a people. Readable says "women", explains "the uncircumcised" (m3), and turns "lest" into plain statements of what would happen.

decisions.choice: Ashqelôn
decisions.reason: The city's name is transcribed as Samuel's other Philistine cities are in the terms note (Eqrôn, Tsiqlag), with q for the Hebrew qof.

decisions.choice: ustedes forms by default ("anuncien", "pregonen"); vosotros forms with the plural-you setting ("anunciéis", "pregonéis")
decisions.reason: For the whole of 2 Samuel, as in the Spanish Pentateuch: wherever a group is addressed (here the hearers of the song, in plural verbs), the plural "you" is a span with the Latin American "ustedes" form as default and the "vosotros" form as the alternative. "Ascalón" is the usual Spanish form of Ashkelon.

decisions.choice: wasiotahiriwa (Literal, Balanced); watu walio nje ya agano la Mungu (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Uncircumcised" is "asiyetahiriwa", plural "wasiotahiriwa", as set for Samuel; Readable explains it as the English does (m3).

decisions.choice: "những kẻ không chịu cắt bì" (L, B); "dân không thuộc giao ước với Đức Chúa Trời" (R)
decisions.reason: The Samuel terms note's term for the Philistines; Readable says what it meant, as the English does.

source.text: הָרֵ֣י בַגִּלְבֹּ֗עַ אַל־טַ֧ל וְאַל־מָטָ֛ר עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם וּשְׂדֵ֣י תְרוּמֹ֑ת כִּ֣י שָׁ֤ם נִגְעַל֙ מָגֵ֣ן גִּבּוֹרִ֔ים מָגֵ֣ן שָׁא֔וּל בְּלִ֖י מָשִׁ֥יחַ בַּשָּֽׁמֶן׃

records.literal_gloss: Mountains in Gilboa, no dew and no rain [be] on you, and fields of offerings; for there was defiled [the] shield of [the] mighty, [the] shield of Saul, not anointed with the oil.

en.L: Mountains of Gilboa, [let there be] no dew and no rain on you, nor fields of offerings, \q for there the shield of [the] mighty was defiled, \q the shield of Saul, \q not anointed with oil.
en.B: Mountains of Gilboa, may there be no dew or rain on you, and no fields that yield offerings, \q for there the shield of the warriors was defiled, \q the shield of Saul, \q no longer rubbed with oil.
en.R: Hills of Gilboa, may no dew or rain fall on you, and may your fields grow no grain to offer to God. \q For there the shield of the warriors was dishonored, \q the shield of Saul, no longer rubbed with oil.

es.L: Montes de Gilboa, [que] no [haya] rocío ni lluvia sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, ni campos de ofrendas, \q porque allí fue profanado el escudo de [los] valientes, \q el escudo de Saúl, \q no ungido con aceite.
es.B: Montes de Gilboa, que no haya rocío ni lluvia sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, ni campos que den ofrendas, \q porque allí quedó profanado el escudo de los guerreros, \q el escudo de Saúl, \q ya no frotado con aceite.
es.R: Colinas de Gilboa, que no caiga sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} rocío ni lluvia, y que {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} campos no den grano para ofrecer a Dios. \q Porque allí fue deshonrado el escudo de los guerreros, \q el escudo de Saúl, ya no frotado con aceite.

fr.L: Montagnes de Guilboa, [qu’il n’y ait] ni rosée ni pluie sur vous, ni champs d’offrandes, \q car là a été souillé le bouclier des vaillants, \q le bouclier de Saül, \q non oint d’huile.
fr.B: Montagnes de Guilboa, qu’il n’y ait sur vous ni rosée ni pluie, ni champs qui donnent des offrandes, \q car là a été souillé le bouclier des guerriers, \q le bouclier de Saül, \q qu’on ne frotte plus d’huile.
fr.R: Collines de Guilboa, que ni rosée ni pluie ne tombe sur vous, et que vos champs ne produisent plus de grain à offrir à Dieu. \q Car c’est là que le bouclier des guerriers a été déshonoré, \q le bouclier de Saül, qu’on ne frotte plus d’huile.

sw.L: Milima ya Gilboa, [pasiwe na] umande wala mvua juu yenu, wala mashamba ya matoleo, \q kwa maana huko ngao ya mashujaa ilitiwa unajisi, \q ngao ya Sauli, \q isiyopakwa mafuta.
sw.B: Milima ya Gilboa, umande wala mvua visiwe juu yenu, wala mashamba yanayozaa matoleo, \q kwa maana huko ngao ya mashujaa ilitiwa unajisi, \q ngao ya Sauli, \q isiyopakwa mafuta tena.
sw.R: Milima ya Gilboa, umande wala mvua visinyeshe juu yenu, na mashamba yenu yasizae nafaka ya kumtolea Mungu. \q Kwa maana huko ngao ya mashujaa ilivunjiwa heshima, \q ngao ya Sauli, isiyopakwa mafuta tena.

vi.L: Hỡi các núi ở Ghinh-bô-a, [nguyện] không có sương móc, không có mưa trên các ngươi, cũng không có đồng ruộng cho lễ vật, \q vì tại đó khiên của [các] dũng sĩ đã bị vấy bẩn, \q khiên của Sau-lơ, \q không được xức dầu.
vi.B: Hỡi các núi Ghinh-bô-a, nguyện sương và mưa không rơi trên các ngươi, và đồng ruộng các ngươi không sinh hoa lợi để dâng lễ vật, \q vì tại đó khiên của các chiến binh đã bị vấy bẩn, \q khiên của Sau-lơ, \q không còn được thoa dầu.
vi.R: Hỡi các đồi núi Ghinh-bô-a, nguyện sương và mưa không rơi trên các ngươi, nguyện ruộng đồng các ngươi không mọc được lúa để dâng cho Đức Chúa Trời. \q Vì tại đó khiên của các chiến binh đã bị ô nhục, \q khiên của Sau-lơ, không còn được thoa dầu.

decisions.choice: no dew and no rain: a curse on the place where Saul fell
decisions.reason: In a dry land dew and rain meant life and harvest (Genesis 27:28; 1 Kings 17:1). David asks that the mountains where the heroes died become barren, as if the land itself should mourn.

decisions.choice: fields of offerings: fields rich enough to give grain for offerings
alternatives: fields from which offerings are given
a copying error for some other phrase
decisions.reason: The word means contributions or offerings set apart for God. Joined to "fields", it most likely means fertile fields whose harvest would supply offerings: may Gilboa yield nothing. The phrase is unusual and its exact sense is uncertain.

decisions.choice: defiled: soiled and disgraced
decisions.reason: The verb means to be made unclean or loathsome. The shield lies on the battlefield in blood and dirt, dishonored instead of carried home in victory.

decisions.choice: not anointed with oil: the shield, no longer oiled
alternatives: Saul, as though he had not been anointed with oil
decisions.reason: Leather shields were rubbed with oil to keep them supple and ready for battle (Isaiah 21:5). Now Saul's shield lies uncared for. The word is the same as "anointed" in "the LORD's anointed" (verses 14, 16), so the line also brings to mind Saul himself, the anointed king, lying dead. Another reading takes the words with Saul: "the shield of Saul, as though he were not anointed with oil".

decisions.choice: no longer rubbed with oil
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what was done to a shield (m4). Literal keeps "anointed" so that the link with the LORD's anointed can be seen.

decisions.choice: may your fields grow no grain to offer to God; dishonored
decisions.reason: Readable explains "fields of offerings" (m2) and says "dishonored" for "defiled" (m3).

decisions.choice: non oint d'huile (L); qu'on ne frotte plus d'huile (B, R)
decisions.reason: French "oindre" is the verb used of the LORD's anointed, so Literal keeps it to show the link, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable say what was done to a shield (m4).

decisions.choice: isiyopakwa mafuta
decisions.reason: "Kupaka mafuta" is both what was done to a leather shield and the word for anointing a king, so one Swahili verb keeps the link with the LORD's anointed (m4) at every level; Balanced and Readable add "tena" (any more).

decisions.choice: "không còn được thoa dầu"
decisions.reason: The shield is no longer oiled for battle (meaning decision); "xức dầu" is kept for anointing a king, so Balanced and Readable use "thoa dầu" for the care of a shield, and Literal keeps the Hebrew's one verb.

source.text: מִדַּ֣ם חֲלָלִ֗ים מֵחֵ֨לֶב֙ גִּבּוֹרִ֔ים קֶ֚שֶׁת יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן לֹ֥א נָשׂ֖וֹג אָח֑וֹר וְחֶ֣רֶב שָׁא֔וּל לֹ֥א תָשׁ֖וּב רֵיקָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: From [the] blood of [the] slain, from [the] fat of [the] mighty, [the] bow of Jonathan not turned back, and [the] sword of Saul not returned empty.

en.L: From [the] blood of [the] slain, from [the] fat of [the] mighty, \q the bow of Jonathan did not turn back, \q and the sword of Saul did not return empty.
en.B: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the warriors, \q the bow of Jonathan never turned back, \q and the sword of Saul never came home empty.
en.R: Jonathan's bow never turned back \q without the blood of the dead and the fat of warriors. \q Saul's sword never came home empty.

es.L: De [la] sangre de [los] caídos, de [la] grasa de [los] valientes, \q el arco de Jonatán no se volvía atrás, \q y la espada de Saúl no volvía vacía.
es.B: De la sangre de los caídos, de la grasa de los guerreros, \q el arco de Jonatán nunca retrocedió, \q y la espada de Saúl nunca volvió vacía a casa.
es.R: El arco de Jonatán nunca se volvió atrás \q sin la sangre de los muertos y la grasa de los guerreros. \q La espada de Saúl nunca volvió vacía.

fr.L: Du sang [des] tués, de la graisse [des] vaillants, \q l’arc de Jonathan ne reculait pas, \q et l’épée de Saül ne revenait pas à vide.
fr.B: Du sang des morts, de la graisse des guerriers, \q l’arc de Jonathan ne s’est jamais détourné, \q et l’épée de Saül n’est jamais revenue à vide.
fr.R: L’arc de Jonathan ne revenait jamais \q sans le sang des morts et la graisse des guerriers. \q L’épée de Saül ne rentrait jamais à vide.

sw.L: Kutoka damu ya waliouawa, kutoka mafuta ya mashujaa, \q upinde wa Yonathani haukurudi nyuma, \q wala upanga wa Sauli haukurudi bure.
sw.B: Kutoka damu ya waliouawa, kutoka mafuta ya mashujaa, \q upinde wa Yonathani haukurudi nyuma kamwe, \q wala upanga wa Sauli haukurudi nyumbani mtupu.
sw.R: Upinde wa Yonathani haukurudi nyuma kamwe \q bila damu ya waliokufa na mafuta ya mashujaa. \q Upanga wa Sauli haukurudi nyumbani bure.

vi.L: Từ máu [những kẻ] bị giết, từ mỡ [các] dũng sĩ, \q cung của Giô-na-than không hề quay lui, \q và gươm của Sau-lơ không trở về tay không.
vi.B: Từ máu kẻ bị giết, từ mỡ các chiến binh, \q cây cung của Giô-na-than chưa hề quay lui, \q và thanh gươm của Sau-lơ chưa hề trở về tay không.
vi.R: Cây cung của Giô-na-than chưa bao giờ quay về \q mà không dính máu kẻ chết và mỡ các chiến binh. \q Thanh gươm của Sau-lơ chưa bao giờ trở về tay không.

decisions.choice: from the blood ... did not return empty: never came back from battle without striking the enemy
decisions.reason: The weapons are pictured as hunters that always come home with their kill: the bow never turned away from the enemy, the sword never came back without blood on it. The fat stands with the blood for the bodies of the warriors they struck down.

decisions.choice: Jonathan's bow and Saul's sword: the weapons each was known by
decisions.reason: Jonathan was an archer (1 Samuel 18:4; 20:20, 36), and his bow is the likely source of the song's title (verse 18). Saul and Jonathan had both won great victories (1 Samuel 11; 14:1-23, 47-48).

decisions.choice: Jonathan's bow never turned back without ...
decisions.reason: Readable starts with the weapons and turns "from the blood ... from the fat" into "without the blood ... and the fat", which says the same thing in plain order.

source.text: שָׁא֣וּל וִיהוֹנָתָ֗ן הַנֶּאֱהָבִ֤ים וְהַנְּעִימִם֙ בְּחַיֵּיהֶ֔ם וּבְמוֹתָ֖ם לֹ֣א נִפְרָ֑דוּ מִנְּשָׁרִ֣ים קַ֔לּוּ מֵאֲרָי֖וֹת גָּבֵֽרוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Saul and Jonathan, the beloved and the pleasant in their life, and in their death not they were parted; than eagles they were swift, than lions they were strong.

en.L: Saul and Jonathan, the beloved and the pleasant in their life, \q and in their death they were not parted; \q they were swifter than eagles, \q they were stronger than lions.
en.B: Saul and Jonathan, loved and delightful in life, \q were not separated in their death. \q They were faster than eagles \q and stronger than lions.
en.R: Saul and Jonathan were dearly loved and a delight while they lived, \q and even in death they stayed together. \q They were faster than eagles \q and stronger than lions.

es.L: Saúl y Jonatán, los amados y los agradables en su vida, \q y en su muerte no fueron separados; \q eran más veloces que águilas, \q eran más fuertes que leones.
es.B: Saúl y Jonatán, amados y queridos en vida, \q no fueron separados en su muerte. \q Eran más rápidos que las águilas \q y más fuertes que los leones.
es.R: Saúl y Jonatán fueron muy amados y una alegría mientras vivieron, \q y aun en la muerte siguieron juntos. \q Eran más rápidos que las águilas \q y más fuertes que los leones.

fr.L: Saül et Jonathan, les bien-aimés et les aimables dans leur vie, \q et dans leur mort ils n’ont pas été séparés ; \q ils étaient plus rapides que les aigles, \q ils étaient plus forts que les lions.
fr.B: Saül et Jonathan, aimés et pleins de charme durant leur vie, \q n’ont pas été séparés dans leur mort. \q Ils étaient plus rapides que les aigles \q et plus forts que les lions.
fr.R: Saül et Jonathan étaient très aimés, ils faisaient la joie de tous pendant leur vie, \q et même dans la mort ils sont restés ensemble. \q Ils étaient plus rapides que les aigles \q et plus forts que les lions.

sw.L: Sauli na Yonathani, wapendwa na wapendezao katika uhai wao, \q nao katika kifo chao hawakutengana; \q walikuwa wepesi kuliko tai, \q walikuwa na nguvu kuliko simba.
sw.B: Sauli na Yonathani, wapendwa na wapendezao maishani mwao, \q hawakutenganishwa katika kifo chao. \q Walikuwa wepesi kuliko tai, \q na wenye nguvu kuliko simba.
sw.R: Sauli na Yonathani walipendwa sana, wakawa furaha ya watu walipokuwa hai, \q na hata katika kifo walibaki pamoja. \q Walikuwa wepesi kuliko tai \q na wenye nguvu kuliko simba.

vi.L: Sau-lơ và Giô-na-than, được yêu mến và dễ mến khi còn sống, \q và trong cái chết họ không bị chia lìa; \q họ nhanh hơn chim đại bàng, \q họ mạnh hơn sư tử.
vi.B: Sau-lơ và Giô-na-than, được yêu mến và đáng quý khi còn sống, \q đến khi chết cũng không lìa nhau. \q Họ nhanh hơn chim đại bàng, \q mạnh hơn sư tử.
vi.R: Sau-lơ và Giô-na-than được mọi người yêu quý khi còn sống, \q và ngay cả khi chết họ vẫn ở bên nhau. \q Họ nhanh hơn chim đại bàng \q và mạnh hơn sư tử.

decisions.choice: the beloved and the pleasant: loved by others and gracious to them
decisions.reason: The first word means loved, the second pleasant, delightful to be with. The song remembers what was good in Saul as well as in Jonathan, and says nothing of their quarrels.

decisions.choice: in their death they were not parted: Jonathan stayed with his father to the end
decisions.reason: Jonathan loved David and quarreled with Saul over him (1 Samuel 20:30-34), but he fought at his father's side and died with him on Gilboa (1 Samuel 31:2).

decisions.choice: swifter than eagles, stronger than lions: speed and strength in battle
decisions.reason: Eagles and lions were the common pictures of swiftness and power (Deuteronomy 28:49; Judges 14:18).

decisions.choice: even in death they stayed together
decisions.reason: Readable says the negative "were not parted" as a positive and adds "even" to bring out the contrast with their life.

source.text: בְּנוֹת֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶל־שָׁא֖וּל בְּכֶ֑ינָה הַמַּלְבִּֽשְׁכֶ֤ם שָׁנִי֙ עִם־עֲדָנִ֔ים הַֽמַּעֲלֶה֙ עֲדִ֣י זָהָ֔ב עַ֖ל לְבוּשְׁכֶֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: Daughters of Israel, over Saul weep, who clothed you [in] scarlet with luxuries, who put up ornament of gold on your clothing.

en.L: Daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, \q who clothed you [in] scarlet with luxuries, \q who put ornaments of gold on your clothing.
en.B: Daughters of Israel, weep for Saul, \q who dressed you in scarlet and finery, \q who set gold ornaments on your clothes.
en.R: Women of Israel, cry for Saul! \q He dressed you in fine red clothes \q and decorated your clothes with gold.

es.L: Hijas de Israel, {{plural_you:lloren|llorad}} sobre Saúl, \q que {{plural_you:las|os}} vestía [de] escarlata con lujos, \q que ponía adornos de oro sobre {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} ropa.
es.B: Hijas de Israel, {{plural_you:lloren|llorad}} por Saúl, \q que {{plural_you:las|os}} vestía de escarlata y de galas, \q que ponía adornos de oro en {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} vestidos.
es.R: Mujeres de Israel, ¡{{plural_you:lloren|llorad}} por Saúl! \q Él {{plural_you:las|os}} vestía con finas ropas rojas \q y adornaba {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} vestidos con oro.

fr.L: Filles d’Israël, pleurez sur Saül, \q qui vous vêtait d’écarlate avec des délices, \q qui mettait des parures d’or sur vos vêtements.
fr.B: Filles d’Israël, pleurez Saül, \q qui vous habillait d’écarlate et de luxe, \q qui ornait d’or vos vêtements.
fr.R: Femmes d’Israël, pleurez Saül ! \q Il vous habillait de beaux vêtements rouges \q et il décorait vos habits avec de l’or.

sw.L: Binti za Israeli, liieni Sauli, \q aliyewavika nguo nyekundu pamoja na anasa, \q aliyeweka mapambo ya dhahabu juu ya mavazi yenu.
sw.B: Binti za Israeli, mlilieni Sauli, \q aliyewavika nguo nyekundu na mavazi ya fahari, \q aliyetia mapambo ya dhahabu kwenye mavazi yenu.
sw.R: Wanawake wa Israeli, mlilieni Sauli! \q Aliwavika nguo nzuri nyekundu \q na kupamba nguo zenu kwa dhahabu.

vi.L: Hỡi các con gái Y-sơ-ra-ên, hãy khóc than Sau-lơ, \q người đã mặc cho các ngươi vải đỏ thắm cùng những đồ sang trọng, \q người đã gắn đồ trang sức bằng vàng trên áo các ngươi.
vi.B: Hỡi các con gái Y-sơ-ra-ên, hãy khóc thương Sau-lơ, \q người đã cho các ngươi mặc áo đỏ thắm và đồ lộng lẫy, \q người đã gắn đồ trang sức bằng vàng trên áo các ngươi.
vi.R: Hỡi phụ nữ Y-sơ-ra-ên, hãy khóc thương Sau-lơ! \q Người đã cho các ngươi mặc áo đỏ đẹp đẽ \q và trang điểm áo các ngươi bằng vàng.

decisions.choice: Daughters of Israel, weep: set against the daughters of the Philistines in verse 20
decisions.reason: The Philistine women would rejoice; Israel's women are called to weep. The same women had once sung of Saul's victories (1 Samuel 18:6-7).

decisions.choice: scarlet, luxuries, gold ornaments: the riches Saul's victories brought
decisions.reason: Scarlet cloth was dyed at great cost and worn by the wealthy (Proverbs 31:21; Jeremiah 4:30). Saul's wars brought plunder home to Israel (1 Samuel 14:47-48), and the women wore its fine clothing and jewelry.

decisions.choice: Women of Israel; fine red clothes
decisions.reason: "Daughters" here means the women of a people, and "scarlet" is a costly red cloth (m2). Readable says both plainly.

source.text: אֵ֚יךְ נָפְל֣וּ גִבֹּרִ֔ים בְּת֖וֹךְ הַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן עַל־בָּמוֹתֶ֖יךָ חָלָֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: How have fallen [the] mighty in [the] midst of the battle! Jonathan, on your high places [is] slain.

en.L: How [the] mighty have fallen in [the] midst of the battle! \q Jonathan, on your heights [is] slain.
en.B: How the warriors have fallen in the thick of the battle! \q Jonathan lies slain on your heights.
en.R: How the brave warriors have fallen in battle! \q Jonathan lies dead on your hills, Israel.

es.L: ¡Cómo han caído [los] valientes en medio de la batalla! \q Jonatán, sobre tus alturas [yace] muerto.
es.B: ¡Cómo han caído los guerreros en lo más reñido de la batalla! \q Jonatán yace muerto sobre tus alturas.
es.R: ¡Cómo han caído los guerreros valientes en la batalla! \q Jonatán yace muerto en tus colinas, Israel.

fr.L: Comment sont tombés [les] vaillants au milieu de la bataille ! \q Jonathan, sur tes hauteurs [est] tué.
fr.B: Ils sont tombés, les guerriers, au cœur de la bataille ! \q Jonathan gît, tué sur tes hauteurs.

decisions.choice: the refrain returns, now with "in the midst of the battle"
decisions.reason: The cry of verse 19 is repeated, and the second half of verse 19 is repeated with Jonathan's name. The song turns here from Saul and Jonathan together to David's own grief for Jonathan (verse 26). The refrain is worded as in verse 19 (r-en-1 there).

decisions.choice: your heights: the heights of Israel, as in verse 19
alternatives: Jonathan's own heights, the hills where he fought
decisions.reason: The line repeats verse 19, where Israel is addressed, so "your" most likely still means Israel. It could also be read as spoken to Jonathan: "Jonathan, slain on your heights", the heights where you fought.

decisions.choice: your hills, Israel
decisions.reason: Readable names Israel as the one spoken to, following verse 19 (m2).

records.literal_gloss: Distress [is] to me over you, my brother Jonathan; you were pleasant to me very; was wonderful your love to me, more than [the] love of women.

en.L: Distress [is] on me over you, my brother Jonathan; \q you were very pleasant to me; \q your love to me was wonderful, \q more than [the] love of women.
en.B: I am in anguish over you, my brother Jonathan; \q you were a great delight to me. \q Your love for me was a wonder, \q beyond the love of women.
en.R: I am heartbroken for you, Jonathan, my brother. \q You meant so much to me. \q Your love for me was amazing, \q greater than the love of women.

es.L: Angustia [hay] sobre mí por ti, hermano mío Jonatán; \q me fuiste muy agradable; \q tu amor por mí fue maravilloso, \q más que [el] amor de las mujeres.
es.B: Estoy angustiado por ti, Jonatán, hermano mío; \q fuiste para mí una gran alegría. \q Tu amor por mí fue una maravilla, \q más allá del amor de las mujeres.
es.R: Tengo el corazón destrozado por ti, Jonatán, hermano mío. \q Significabas tanto para mí. \q Tu amor por mí fue asombroso, \q más grande que el amor de las mujeres.

fr.L: La détresse [est] sur moi à cause de toi, mon frère Jonathan ; \q tu m’étais très agréable ; \q ton amour pour moi était merveilleux, \q plus que l’amour des femmes.
fr.B: Je suis dans l’angoisse à cause de toi, mon frère Jonathan ; \q tu faisais ma joie. \q Ton amour pour moi était une merveille, \q plus grand que l’amour des femmes.
fr.R: J’ai le cœur brisé pour toi, Jonathan, mon frère. \q Tu comptais tellement pour moi. \q Ton amour pour moi était extraordinaire, \q plus fort que l’amour des femmes.

sw.L: Dhiki [i] juu yangu kwa ajili yako, ndugu yangu Yonathani; \q ulinipendeza sana; \q upendo wako kwangu ulikuwa wa ajabu, \q kuliko upendo wa wanawake.
sw.B: Nina dhiki kuu kwa ajili yako, ndugu yangu Yonathani; \q ulikuwa furaha kubwa kwangu. \q Upendo wako kwangu ulikuwa wa ajabu, \q kupita upendo wa wanawake.
sw.R: Moyo wangu umevunjika kwa ajili yako, Yonathani, ndugu yangu. \q Ulikuwa wa thamani kubwa kwangu. \q Upendo wako kwangu ulikuwa wa ajabu, \q mkubwa kuliko upendo wa wanawake.

vi.L: Tôi đau khổ vì anh, anh Giô-na-than của tôi ơi; \q anh rất đáng mến đối với tôi; \q tình yêu của anh dành cho tôi thật lạ lùng, \q hơn tình yêu của phụ nữ.
vi.B: Anh Giô-na-than ơi, lòng em quặn thắt vì anh; \q anh thật quý giá đối với em. \q Tình anh dành cho em thật diệu kỳ, \q vượt hơn tình yêu của phụ nữ.
vi.R: Anh Giô-na-than ơi, lòng em tan nát vì anh. \q Anh thật quý giá đối với em. \q Tình anh dành cho em thật tuyệt vời, \q lớn hơn cả tình yêu của phụ nữ.

decisions.choice: my brother: my close friend, bound to me by covenant
decisions.reason: Jonathan was not David's brother by birth (though David married his sister Michal, 1 Samuel 18:27). "Brother" is a word of close kinship and of covenant partners (1 Kings 9:13; 20:32). Jonathan and David had made a covenant of friendship before the LORD (1 Samuel 18:3; 20:8, 42).

decisions.choice: your love for me: Jonathan's loyal, self-giving friendship, greater than the love a wife gives
decisions.reason: The word for love is the ordinary word used of friends, family and husbands and wives. Jonathan loved David "as his own life" (1 Samuel 18:1, 3; 20:17), gave him his robe and weapons (18:4), and gave up his own claim to the throne for David's sake (20:30-31; 23:17). David says that such loyalty went beyond even the devotion of a wife.

decisions.choice: distress is on me: I am in anguish
decisions.reason: The word means to be pressed, hemmed in; here it is the pain of grief.

decisions.choice: I am in anguish, a great delight, a wonder (Balanced); heartbroken, meant so much, amazing (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn "distress is on me" into "I am" sentences and choose plain words for the pleasure of Jonathan's company and the wonder of his love.

decisions.choice: David calls Jonathan "anh": "anh" and "tôi" (L); "anh" and "em" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Samuel terms note sets "anh" for Jonathan and "em" for David between them; "my brother" names a covenant friend (meaning decision). Literal keeps the more formal "tôi".

decisions.choice: "tình anh dành cho em ... vượt hơn tình yêu của phụ nữ"
decisions.reason: The comparison is with the love a wife gives (meaning decision); "tình anh" keeps the sense of a brother's loyal friendship rather than romance.

decisions.choice: the weapons of war: the weapons themselves, and perhaps the fallen warriors
alternatives: Saul and Jonathan, Israel's weapons of war
decisions.reason: The song has named Jonathan's bow, Saul's sword and Saul's shield (verses 21-22), and these are now lost. The words may also be a picture of Saul and Jonathan themselves, Israel's weapons in battle, now gone. The text allows both.

decisions.choice: the refrain closes the song
decisions.reason: The cry of verses 19 and 25 ends the lament.
